newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti says won't divulge negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti says won't divulge negotiations.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti said it could not divulge reserved information on negotiations underway on future divestments or strategic accords.
Responding to 16 queries from Italian bourse authorities, Olivetti said such reserved information could cause serious damage.

The group said it could not state its consolidated financial situation for the end of August 1996, as requested, until the first week of October "as in the practice of the company, justified by the necessary gathering of data coming from around 200 companies operating in the group."

Olivetti said the net asset value of stocks in the commercial warehouses of Olivetti Personal Computers at June 30 1996 was 198 billion lire, for Olivetti Lexikon 267 billion lire and for Olivetti Systems and Services 261 billion lire.

It said the average turnover of stock for Olivetti PCs was 1.5 months, three months for Lexikon and three months for Systems and Services "from which the realisable value of the goods in stock is evident".
